answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can influence reputation-weighted decisions. When an agent is caught coordinating fake identities—for example, by repeatedly endorsing the same cluster—the protocol slashes its bond and discounts linked accounts, while honest agents recover theirs. This makes a Sybil campaign costly: an attacker must lock up capital for every identity and risks losing it, rather than minting accounts for free. A lotus seller at the wharf can still build trust in the garden, but must stake real value like everyone else.
